sentences.text: This is a claim petition filed by the petitioner claiming compensation of .1,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the injuries sustained by him.

2. The case of the petitioner in brief is that on 27.08.2022 at about 4.00 p.m., the petitioner was proceeding in an Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.AP-39- W-6140 while going towards Mulbagal side from Bangarupalem driven by S.Shakeer Basha on the left side of Bengaluru-Chennai NH Road and when they reached near Thatireddipalli Cross, on Gangavaram Mandal, Chittoor District, Andra Pradesh, one Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A-7108, driven by its driver at high speed in a rash and negligent manner, suddenly came to the left side of road and abruptly stopped the lorry in front of autorickshaw due to which the autorickshaw collided to the lorry resulting in accident.
Due to the accident, petitioner sustained grievous injuries.

Thereafter, the petitioner was shifted to Govt.
Hospital, Palamaner Hospital, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and spent a sum of .1,05,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charges.
Prior to the accident
, the petitioner was hale and healthy and was a Mason by profession and earning .25,000/- per month.
Due to the accidental injuries, he suffered permanent disability.
The accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of tipper lorry by its driver.
The respondents, being the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
3. Upon service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appear before the tribunal, hence he has been placed as exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared before the tribunal through the counsel and filed the written statement.
4. In the Written Statement, the respondent No.2 denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.
The respondent No.2 also denied age, occupation and income of petitioner as well as place, time and manner of accident.
Further contended that the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts and same is liable to be dismissed.

Further contended that at the time of accident, this respondent has not at all issued any policy in respect of Trailer Truck bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A- 7108 Engine No:400952D0058488 Chassis No:
MEC2416BCJP058653 Make Bhara Benz Goods Carrier.
Further contended that the vehicle involved in the accident is Tipper Lorry whereas the policy obtained by owner under policy No.OG-23-1701-1802-00212702 is for the two wheeler.
Further this insurance company has not received the premium to cover tipper lorry from the owner of said tipper lorry involved in the accident.
Further there is no valid insurance in respect of tipper lorry involved in this accident.
The amount claimed by the petitioner is highly exorbitant.
Hence, prayed for dismissal of petition.

sentences.text:
On the basis of above pleadings, the learned predecessor in office framed the following:
ISSUES 1.

Whether petitioner proves that, he sustained grievous injuries in the accident that occurred on 27.08.2022 at about 04.00 p.m., near Thatireddipalli Cross,
Gangavaram Mandal, Chittoor District, while he was proceeding in a Autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.AP-39-W- 6140, due to the rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A-7108 by its driver?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed in the claim petition?

If so, what is the quantum of compensation and from whom?
3.
What order or award?
6. In order to prove the contention of the petition, the petitioner examined himself as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.6 and closed his side of evidence.
On the other hand, the respondent insurance company examined its Assistant manager as RW.1 and got marked documents marked at Ex.R.1 to 3(a) and closed his side of evidence.

7. Heard the arguments on both the sides and perused the materials available on record.
8.

Findings of this tribunal on the above issues are as under:-
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
 Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative;
 Issue No.3 : As per final order for the  following:-
 -:REASONS:-
9. Issue No.1:- The petitioner contended that on 27.08.2022 at about 04.00 p.m., accident was caused near Thatireddipalli Cross, Gangavaram Mandal, Chittoor District, while he was proceeding in a autorickshaw bearing Regn.No.AP-39-W-6140, due to the rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A-7108 by its driver in which he sustained grievous injuries.
10.
In order to prove rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A-7108 by its driver, the petitioner got examined himself as PW.1.
In the chief examination, PW.1 deposed that due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A-7108 by its driver the accident occurred.
Though PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondent, nothing to dispute or Mahaboob Shariff vs Paramjit Kaur on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44368837/

sentences.text: 3 doubt the contention of petitioner related to the accident could be elicited during the cross.
11. Further, in order to prove the accident, the petitioner produced first information statement and its translated copy which is marked as Ex.P.2 and P.2(a).
Based on the first information statement lodged before the police, the police registered the FIR as per Ex.P.1.

On perusal of Ex.P.2 and P.2(a),
first information statement, one of the relative has lodged a complaint with the police on 28.08.2022 pertaining to the accident occurred on 27.08.2022.
In the first information statement as well as FIR, the accident is stated to have been caused due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
The accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The petitioner also furnished spot mahazar which is marked as Ex.P.3.
The said document discloses that the police visited the place of incident after registration of FIR and the place of incident is described in the said document.
In the mahazar also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV Report, wherein the damages caused to the vehicle are mentioned.
The said document discloses the aspect of involvement of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The driver or owner of the offending vehicle not provided satisfactory explanation regarding the manner in which damages are caused to the vehicle.
The said document clearly indicates involvement of offending vehicle in the accident.
The I.O., after completion of investigation, filed the final report against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/s.337, 338 of IPC as per Ex.P.5.
In the final report also, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle.
The police filed the final report after detailed investigation.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have questioned the correctness of the investigation.
No satisfactory materials are placed by the respondents to show that the investigation is not conducted in a proper manner.
The driver or owner of offending vehicle does not appear to have challenged or questioned the FIR or final report filed by the police.

In the FIR as well as final report, the accident is stated to have been caused due to negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle which aspect does not appear to have been challenged in any manner.
The respondents not furnished any satisfactory materials to rebut or controvert the documents furnished by petitioner related to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
PW.1 is cross examined on behalf of respondents and in the cross examination also, nothing to disprove or disbelieve the contention of petitioners could be elicited.

No satisfactory materials are being placed before the Tribunal to disprove the contention of petitioner pertaining to the aspect of negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
12. The respondents placed no satisfactory materials before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials to the contrary, the documents furnished by the petitioner are to be considered for ascertaining the aspect of negligence.
The respondents not furnished any materials to show that there is no negligence on the part of driver of offending vehicle in the cause of accident.
The respondents placed nothing before the tribunal to disprove case of petitioner.
On perusal of entire record, it discloses that the driver of insured vehicle has driven the vehicle in a rash and negligent manner that resulted in the accident.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.5, this tribunal is of the opinion that the accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A-7108 by its driver and same has resulted in Mahaboob Shariff vs Paramjit Kaur on 10 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44368837/
4 grievous injuries to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 held in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

In order to assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like injury, pain and suffering sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment and medical attendants, conveyance.
14. The petitioner contended that due to accident he sustained grievous injuries.
In order to prove the injuries, the petitioner produced wound certificate issued by Area Hospital, Palamaner, Chittoor District which is marked as Ex.P.4.
The doctor diagnosed that petitioner sustained 2x0.2 cm laceration on left upper eyelid and 2x1cm laceration on right shoulder.
The doctor opined that injuries are of the petitioner are simple in nature.
The petitioner not produced Discharge Summary to show that he has taken treatment as an inpatient.
In order to prove the disability, the petitioner neither produced disability certificate nor examined the doctor.
The petitioner has also not produced any medical bills.
The petitioner has not examined the doctor to prove the aspect of disability.
In the absence of sufficient and satisfactory materials, it is not possible to ascertain and adjudicate the aspect of disability of petitioner.
So, in the absence of proper evidence, this tribunal cannot award compensation under the head of future loss of income and other heads.

By considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also the injuries sustained by the petitioner,
the petitioner is entitled for Global compensation of .1,00,000/-.
15.

In MFA.No.100090 of 2014 C/w. MFA.No.25107 of 2013 between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Page No.7 at Para No.15 held as follows:
"However, the provisions of Section 149(1) of the Act to the extent they speak of interest payable on the compensation amount is in the nature of an exception to the general law enacted in 169 of the M.V.Act and therefore, the provisions of Section 34 of CPC to that extent become invocable on the general principles of construction of statutes namely the special law overrides the general law.

entities.text: Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others Vs. Ulrich Belchior Fernandes and another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, in the absence of any other law relating to interest on Judgments, the MACT has to follow the provisions of Section 34 of CPC, 1908.

Thus, in the given circumstances of this case,
interest at the rate of more than 6% could not have been awarded."

In view of ratio and dictum laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in the above judgment, the petitioner is entitled for interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
16. The petitioner has filed petition against the respondents No.1 and 2.
It is already held that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of Tipper Lorry bearing Regn.No.OD-28-A-7108 by its driver.

Respondent No.2 contended that the petitioner suppressed material facts and furnished false particulars while obtaining the policy of insurance and the insurance company is not liable to pay compensation as there is violation of terms of policy. Sec.150(2) of IMV Act provides the defence available to the insurance company in a claim petition. Sec.150(2)(b) of the Act states Mahaboob Shariff vs Paramjit Kaur on 10 December, 2024

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/44368837/
5

that the insurance company can raise defence that the policy is void on the ground that it was obtained by nondisclosure of any material fact or by representation of any fact which was false in some material particular.
The respondent No.2 furnished the policy which is marked as Ex.R.1.
On perusal of Ex.R.1, it discloses that the policy pertains to TVS Champ vehicle.
The offending vehicle is a tipper lorry and there appears to be no dispute in that regard.
The policy availed by respondent No.1 does not appear to be pertaining to the Tipper lorry and it pertains to TVS Champ vehicle.
The premium received by respondent No.2 pertains to the Champ vehicle and not to Tipper lorry.
On perusal of said document, it appears that respondent No.1 furnished false particulars of the vehicle while availing the policy.
The description of the vehicle appears to have been mentioned as TVS Champ and not as Tipper lorry.
The amount of premium appears to have been collected related to TVS Champ and not related to Tipper lorry.
Respondent No.1 appears to have availed the policy by non-disclosure of make and model of the vehicle which is a material fact for issue of policy and for calculating the premium.

Respondent No.2 also furnished copy of notice issued to respondent No.1 which is marked as Ex.R.2 which discloses that respondent No.2 called upon respondent No.1 to provide explanation for mentioning wrong description of vehicle information at the time of availing the policy.
The respondent No.1 does not appear to have provided any explanation to the said notice.
Further, respondent No.1, being the owner of offending vehicle, is in a better position to explain about the description of vehicle provided at the time of availing the policy.
The respondent No.1 neither appeared before the Tribunal nor appear to have replied the notice.
Respondent No.1 failed to appear before the Tribunal in spite of service on notice.
No satisfactory explanation provided by respondent No.1 related to the defence taken by respondent No.2.
The materials on record disclose that the policy of insurance pertains to TVS Champ vehicle and not pertains to Tipper lorry.
The premium appears to have been collected pertaining to the Tipper lorry only.
The vehicle involved in the accident is a Tipper lorry, the description of which is not provided in the policy of insurance.
Respondent No.2 succeeded in establishing the defence taken by them in the case.
Respondent No.1 appears to have availed the policy by non-disclosure of material facts, the policy becomes void and there is clear violation of terms and conditions of the policy.
As the policy of insurance is void due to violation of terms and conditions for non-disclosure of material facts, insurance company cannot be fastened with the liability to pay compensation.
So, the respondent No.1, being the owner offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, Issue No.2 answered Partly in the Affirmative.
17. Issue No.3:

In view of the findings given on the above said issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following:
O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner Under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation amount of .1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.

Respondent No.1, being the owner of offending vehicle, is liable to pay compensation to petitioner and is directed to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of two months from the date of award.
